title: flapsim (headless deterministic side-scroller, 6 modules, mid-run feature change + docs)
description: A multi-phase build: implement from spec, write tests, review own code and cite real file:line, emit a deterministic artifact, then receive a mid-run user request for a cross-cutting feature plus documentation that must quote real signatures. Designed to create many natural opportunities to revisit files the agent itself produced.
notes: Constants are invented (gravity 18, an LCG, a clean-glide bonus) so the model has no priors to answer from and must consult the spec and its own code.
Every seed file is under 1900 chars so a read leaves a COMPLETE resident copy; the harness clips tool output at 2000 and a clipped read makes any 'it is above in this conversation' claim false.
Verification is routed through --selfcheck rather than `unittest` because unittest prints a timing line that varies between runs, so two identical runs never compare equal.

Phases are SEPARATE USER TURNS, not one message. A single message asking for all five phases made the model produce 141,497 chars of reasoning and never call a write tool — 26 minutes to write nothing. The SWE-bench pilot reaches a 121k-token peak on this same model and harness and completes, so the limit was the over-stuffed prompt, not the model. Splitting also matches how work really arrives from a user.
status: RETIRED — do not use for re-reference experiments
retired_because: Completability and re-reference pull against each other here. The single-message form made the agent re-read constantly and complete nothing; the six-turn form completes the work correctly (29/40, 12/12 held-out) and produces almost no re-reads — 19 reads across 18 distinct files, 1 read twice. A live four-arm run was VOID: 1 would-fire event and 0 substitutions across 44 turns. Superseded for this purpose by the SWE-bench 10-problem baseline. See U17 in reports/session-handoff.md.
